Title: Shadow of the Beast / Aggravated Damage

Messages.Author: -< Johann Lionheart >-
Messages.Body:
Here is the combat sequence...

1. Bum Rush
2. Shadow of the Beast
3. Wolf Claws
4. Strike for 2 Agg
5. Strike for 2 mor Agg
6. Resolve Damage

The first point of Agg sends the person to Torpor... then the rest of
the damage is resolved by burning blood counters... so which is true?

1. Person loses 3 blood counters all of which are Agg?
2. Person loses 2 blood counters all of which are Agg because of the
two different strikes at +1 agg each?

Is only the first point of Agg per combat not resolved by spending a
blood or is it the first point of Agg per stirke?

Thanks!

Messages.Author: LSJ
Messages.Body:


The combatant receiving the 2 agg damage in the first resolution phase
must handle the two points of agg damage (assuming he doesn't prevent
the damage). Every point of damage done must be handled.

The first point of agg damage wounds him (since agg damage cannot be healed).
The second point, also unhealable, has an additional effect now that the
vampire is wounded: the point of agg damage will burn him unless he burns
a blood. So he burns 1 blood.

Now all damage is handled, and the vampire is no longer ready. So combat
ends. The remaining, as-yet-undeclared additional strike is never chosen
or resolved.

Net result: the vampire burns 1 blood and goes to torpor.

See 6.4.3 and 6.4.6 of the rules for complete details.

If you're talking about Shadow of the Wolf (I assume that's what you meant,
Shadow of the Beast is an action), remember that the +1 strength is only on
the additional strike. So it would be 1 agg, then 2 agg.
But unless the first 1 agg was prevented/dodged/avoided, you couldn't use an
additional strike, since the opposing vampire is in torpor and combat
ends before additional strikes are announced.

"-< Johann Lionheart >-" <Johann@/nospam/johannsdomain.com> wrote:
> Yes I meant Shadow of the Wolf
> Why would combat end after the first strike? We didn't get to the
> damage resolution phase? Does this mean that you can not press to do
> more damage if the vamp is already going to torpor?

Vampires in torpor can't be in combat.
And damage resolves when the strike resolves.
If that damage sends the vampire to torpor, then the combat must end
immediately. So, no. You don't get additional strikes, and you can't
press to continue. Unless a card effect [like Undead Persistence, for
example] contradicts the rules.
